command: node benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/record-new-task-dedupe.mjs --tree <exact export of b6f10295a with node_modules>

coreNotCompared.reply.subscription: the core's subscription to the session's feed (`thread/start` subscribes its caller); Node's host keeps its feed inside the process
coreNotCompared.reply.thread.activityAt: the core's thread summary (`thread/start`'s `thread`), whose Node counterpart is the snapshot the recording does not hold (see `notCompared`)
coreNotCompared.reply.thread.title: as `reply.thread.activityAt`
coreNotCompared.reply.turn: the first turn the attempt started (`thread/start`'s `turn`); Node's turn starts in its daemon's `submit`, a model in the recording, whose answer the recording does not hold

comparison.method: each scenario whole: its `steps`, and for every recorded step everything in the recording except the paths of `notCompared`; the core's side is built as `translated` states, and both sides are normalised only as `normalised` states

normalised.fresh session address: numbered `<fresh:N>` by first appearance in the scenario on both sides (see `random`)
normalised.key order: objects are compared without regard to key order (the recording is written with sorted keys); arrays in order
normalised.thread.id: the core's session address in `thread.id` is the reply's `sessionId` (see `translated`)

notCompared.recorded[].daemonCalls: Node's calls from the desktop host to its daemon client inside one request (create, configure, submit, unsubscribe, read; the daemon is a model, leg.mjs): the core runs these steps inside its own `thread/start` with no wire between them. What they do is compared through `sessions` (a session made, given its prompt, or removed again) and `receipts`
notCompared.recorded[].reply.errno: a field of the Node fs error the leg catches in the host's own process (io-error): libuv's number for the error, which differs by operating system (UV_EISDIR is -4068 on Windows, -21 on Linux: libuv include/uv/errno.h), and which no Node caller receives across a process (the window's IPC rejection carries the message; the phone's remote call the message and code). The core's rejection is a protocol `domainError` with a code and a message (mixdog-app-protocol ErrorData), which the desktop turns into an Error with `code` (apps/desktop/src/main/protocol/core-error.ts:17-22): no field of it carries an errno
notCompared.recorded[].reply.snapshot: Node's answer carries the session snapshot its daemon returned (session-host-lifecycle.ts:922,951: the leg's daemon model, leg.mjs `full`, with the host's remote fields): the recording has no real one. The core's answer has no snapshot (its session state travels on the subscription's feed)
notCompared.recorded[].reply.syscall: as `recorded[].reply.errno`: the name of the fs call inside Node (`read`), a field of the same in-process error object only

translated.recorded[].receipts: the files of `<userdata>/new-task-receipts`, by name, byte for byte (latin1), as the recorder reads them
translated.recorded[].reply: `submitNewTask` through the desktop's service lane (service-route.ts: `thread/start`), as received on both sides (`asReceived`): an answer is compared with `thread.id` as `sessionId` and `accepted: true` (the core answers only a started task, Node's `accepted` answer), less the paths of `coreNotCompared`; a rejection is its message and every own field of the error on both sides; a crash step's reply is `{crashed: at}` on both sides
translated.recorded[].sessions: every thread `thread/list` lists, with `prompts` = its `userMessage` items (`thread/items/list`) and `reserved` = no prompt yet (Node's daemon model sets `reserved` false exactly when it records a prompt, leg.mjs `submit`, and removes a reserved session without one on `unsubscribe`)
translated.recorded[].step: the step the replay drives (scenarios.mjs), the same list the recording ran

daemon: the daemon is a model (leg.mjs) of the rules the new-task path uses; its calls are recorded for Node only
processes: each scenario runs its legs in a Windows job of its own (lib/process-job.mjs): every process a leg starts is ended with it, and a leg that leaves one running fails

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

random.fresh session address: a session address after a refusal reset or a changed-content retry is `sess_desktop_` + 32 random bytes in hex (freshSessionId, new-task-requests.ts:85); numbered `<fresh:N>` by first appearance in a scenario
